speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: Whereas May 19th is National Hepatitis Testing Day, and July 28 is World Hepatitis Testing Day.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: Hepatitis C is recognized as the most common blood borne viral infection in the United States.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: WHEREAS, Hepatitis C has infected an estimated 70,000 Coloradans and as many as 4 million American residents, nearly one in 50 persons and more than 130 people I'm sorry, 130 million people worldwide.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: Whereas, it is the leading cause of cirrhosis and liver cancer and the number one reason for liver transplants in the United States.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: Whereas, more Americans die of hepatitis C than from HIV making Hepatitis C one of the top preventable causes of death in the United States.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: Whereas, many, as many as 17,000 hepatitis C related deaths occur annually in the United States, these rates are expected to peak between the years 2030 and 2035 at 36,000 deaths per year .

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: WHEREAS, people born between 1945 and 1965 are five times more likely to be infected than any other adults.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: More than 75% of all people with hepatitis C in the United States are people in this age age range, and many remain unaware of their status because they have not been tested for the virus.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: WHEREAS, the incidence of hepatitis C disproportionately affects people of color.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: Whereas, 75% of infected persons do not show any signs or symptoms leading to the website to the hepatitis C virus to cause poor health outcomes and be labeled as, quote unquote, the silent epidemic.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: WHEREAS, the majority of individuals living with hepatitis C infection can be cured of the virus through the advent of effective treatment options currently available on the market and those cured through the treatment are able to stop and even reverse damage to the liver caused by the virus.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: WHEREAS, Hepatitis C treatment costs are less than one fifth the cost of liver transplants.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: WHEREAS, Hepatitis C can be prevented, testing can identify existing infections, and early diagnosis and treatment can save lives, money and resources.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: Whereas, Hep C connection is available as a statewide resource for education testing, linkage to care and other support services.

speaker: Councilman Lopez
raw_text: Now, therefore, be it proclaimed by the Council of the City and County of Denver, Section one, the Denver City Council agrees that preventing and treating hepatitis C is an important public health initiative that will improve the quality of life for Denver residents affected by the virus.
